sec: Ciliopathy overview: cilia function & types · p786

opts: Hereditary cystic disorders of the kidney caused by a tubular epithelium defect
Acquired cystic diseases of the kidney arising after middle age
Glomerular diseases due to podocyte injury
items.exp: Ciliopathies are hereditary cystic disorders of the kidney: cilia maintain the differentiated phenotype of tubular epithelium, and a defect causes cysts. (Book p786)

items.q: Fill up: Cilia maintain the differentiated phenotype of ______ epithelium.
items.exp: Cilia function: maintain the differentiated phenotype of tubular epithelium, and this function is regulated by polycystin. (Book p786)

items.q: A defect in the cilia of renal tubular epithelium leads to which structural consequence?
opts: Loss of the differentiated phenotype with cyst formation
Diffuse thickening of the glomerular basement membrane
Thrombotic microangiopathy with fragmented red cells
items.exp: Defect of cilia → ciliopathies: the tubular epithelium loses its differentiated phenotype and cysts develop. (Book p786)

items.q: The function of cilia in tubular epithelium is regulated by:
items.exp: Cilia function — maintaining the differentiated phenotype of tubular epithelium — is regulated by polycystin. (Book p786)

items.q: Match the four types in the ciliopathy flowchart — 1) ADPKD  2) ARPKD  3) Juvenile nephronophthisis  4) MCDK … A) Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease  B) Medullary cystic disease of kidney  C) Juvenile nephronophthisis  D) Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease
items.exp: The TYPES flowchart lists four ciliopathies: ADPKD, ARPKD, juvenile nephronophthisis and medullary cystic disease of kidney (MCDK). (Book p786)

items.q: Which entity is NOT one of the four ciliopathies listed in the TYPES flowchart?
items.exp: Medullary sponge kidney is later described as 'not a ciliopathy' — an acquired disease; the four ciliopathies listed are ADPKD, ARPKD, juvenile nephronophthisis and MCDK. (Book p786)
